contexts.text: They believe that conjugial love... flows forth from a certain natural instinct, as they call it.
They see... that brute animals act from instinct...
They are carried as by blind instinct into the exercises of charity.
For beasts follow their affection from instinct without reason.
Evil Spirits... know how to do this from a kind of instinct...
This knowledge is said to be connate, and is called instinct; but it is of the love in which (these animals) are.
Besides other wonderful things, which are called instinct.
Our husbands liken this to instinct...
At once, as from a kind of instinct, they know that they are mates... It is said as from fate, instinct, and dictate, and it is meant from the Divine Providence. CL 316:3.
(With animals) this is instinct.
Without this separation (of the understanding from the will)... man could not act from reason, but from instinct.
A beast does not know and understand what it is doing; and yet it acts; for it acts from influx from the Spiritual World; and such act is instinct.
Every (animal) is Known from its own essence or nature. From this, and according to this, is the instinct of each.
This influx from the Spiritual World is what is called instinct; and it is called instinct because it comes forth without thought as a means. There are also accessories of instinct, from habit.
(These beasts) enjoy no faculty of understanding... but act from instinct, which is excited by their natural love.
Brute animals are carried to natural ends only, and this by a certain impetus, which is called instinct.
Brute animals are carried away to natural good by instinct; and thus from ignorance of truth and good.
From a natural instinct, as it were, Spirits can at once transfer good into evil.
Their natural instinct imbued in the life of the body... [causes them] to be possessed of such a cupidity... that they cannot desist.

Each Spirit has his own instinct of life, which is apperceived when he is either as it were left by himself, or is in the society of his like. But it disappears when he is in the society of better Spirits. I have perceived this variety; and also that he has been suddenly brought back to his natural instinct...

They who desire to be the highest in Heaven... are deprived of all rationality... They do not know what they are doing: they do everything from instinct; and as if in sleep... As they have supposed that there is something good in such ambition, it is conceded to them to act according to their instinct...

When rationality is taken away from a Spirit, so that he acts solely from instinct, he is excused for whatever he does; for he acts as if in sleep... Whereas, when the same are at the same time rational, their rationality then serves for nothing more than to make them careful to conceal their instinct...

On the left side there is a Hell where there are demons... who act from mere instinct, having been deprived of rationality. Nor are they so evil; for when they are doing evil they suppose that they are doing good... SE 1398:end.
Such Spirits cannot desist... Their nature and instinct drive them to these things.
That the ends in the life of the body induce a nature and instinct, which he carries with him into the other life. Explained.
Such do they become who in the life of the body do nothing except from instinct...
They derive such an instinct from actuality...
He could know the lower minds of all as it were from instinct.

Everyone forms for himself his natural soul; consequently a certain natural instinct as it were; for, after the life of the body. Souls and Spirits are carried along by a kind of instinct to the doing of evil; for, in their soul, from the things acquired by actualities, there is a Natural, which is no otherwise circumstanced that is instinct with animals; with this difference, that the Spirits are able to reason...
This cunning is a Natural which they had acquired, thus a kind of instinct...
But... many... do evil, and that deceitfully, but still from natural instinct... There is a distinction between deceit as an instinct, and deceit as premeditated.
The life (of evil Spirits) is no otherwise than as is the life of wild beasts; for they act from instinct...
That there are such lives with Spirits, which are as it were an instinct remaining from the confirming and thus persuading things of the life of the body...

On spheres, instinct, etc... Every Spirit, and still more every Society of Spirits, exhales a sphere from itself... With evil Genii, from the life of cupidities... which is a sphere as it were of instincts thence...
As Spirits lack memory, they have a sort of instinct as it were, which acts as has been said.
On the instinct of Spirits, and on their memory, and love. Explained.
Spirits have a kind of instinct, which is such that they desire... this or that thing according to their nature and state... SE 4469.
They believe... that all things flow from blind instinct...
He (then) acted as if deprived of mind, acting as it were from instinct.
Into everyone of them is inspired the desire together with the endeavour to go away... to the place destined for himself, thus from instinct, although it appears to them as if they know.
Animals... know from what is innate and implanted, which is called instinct...
The reason is that man is not born with instinct, like a beast.
